claims.text: Adding 1–3 vol% graphene nanoplatelets to CoCrFeNi will enable dual-mode lubrication from room temperature to 800 °C.
The dual-mode lubrication will maintain uniformly low friction throughout the full temperature range.
The dual-mode lubrication will reduce wear throughout the full temperature range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits variable friction and wear behavior over a broad temperature range.
The proposed intervention is to uniformly disperse approximately 1–3 vol% graphene nanoplatelets in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
The proposed test regime uses ambient oxidizing conditions, moderate load, and temperatures of approximately 25, 300, 500, and 800 °C.
Graphene nanoplatelets can be uniformly dispersed in the CoCrFeNi matrix at the proposed loading.
Dispersed graphene nanoplatelets will facilitate formation of an adaptive lubricious tribofilm during sliding.
At room temperature, the low shear strength of graphene's layered structure will reduce friction.
At elevated temperatures, controlled oxidation of graphene or its interaction with the alloy matrix will promote a self-adaptive tribofilm.
The self-adaptive tribofilm will maintain low friction and minimize wear at elevated temperatures up to 800 °C.
Graphene-modified CoCrFeNi will have lower coefficients of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature.
Graphene-modified CoCrFeNi will have lower wear rates than unmodified CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature.
The inconsistent tribological performance of baseline CoCrFeNi is caused by temperature-dependent oxidation and microstructural effects.
Ambient oxidation, moderate sliding loads, and temperatures from about 25 to 800 °C are representative of practical tribological applications.
The stability and long-term durability of the graphene-induced tribofilm under prolonged high-temperature oxidation are uncertain.
